title: Getting started with scholid
text: scholid exposes small set user-facing functions operate consistently across identifier types: scholid_types() lists supported identifier types. is_scholid(x, type) checks whether values match identifier type. normalize_scholid(x, type) returns canonical identifier strings. scholid_key(x, type) returns keys comparing deduplicating identifiers. format_scholid(x, type, ) writes identifiers resolver URLs, CURIEs, arXiv DOIs. extract_scholid(text, type) extracts identifiers free text. locate_scholid(text, types) finds identifiers several types free text, positions. classify_scholid(x) guesses identifier type per element. detect_scholid_type(x) detects identifier types canonical wrapped input values (e.g., URLs labels). generic helpers dispatch internally type-specific implementations is_doi(), normalize_orcid(), extract_isbn().

title: How Scholarly Identifiers Are Defined
text: Text copied PDFs, word processors, web pages often contains characters look like ASCII . scholid handles follows. Invisible characters: soft hyphen (U+00AD), zero-width directional marks (U+200B–U+200F, U+202A–U+202E, U+2060–U+2064, U+2066–U+2069), byte order mark (U+FEFF). never part identifier. is_scholid() returns FALSE values contain one; normalize_scholid(), extract_scholid(), detect_scholid_type() remove first. Unicode spaces: -break space (U+00A0), U+1680, U+2000–U+200A, U+202F, U+205F, ideographic space (U+3000). count whitespace wherever ASCII space : trimmed, may follow label separate digit groups, end match extraction. identifier contains one, is_scholid() returns FALSE. Unicode dashes (U+2010–U+2013, U+2212, U+FE63, U+FF0D) full-width digits (U+FF10–U+FF19): normalize_scholid(), extract_scholid(), detect_scholid_type() read - 0–9 types table . is_scholid() classify_scholid() accept ASCII characters. em dash (U+2014) never read hyphen. Dashes read hyphens types separate digit groups hyphens. free text, en dash usually marks page year range, 1998–2003 passes ISSN checksum, extract_scholid() doesn’t read dashes ISSN. DOI suffix may contain Unicode character, ARK names, SWHID qualifiers, RRID bodies free-form, types keep dashes digits written.
